title: fleet upgrade drops worktrees and dependency checkouts without a row or a count
body:
Found by the 2026-09-21 doc audit (finding K5).

`fleet upgrade` dropped worktrees and dependency checkouts that carry a runtime without a row or a count: `estate_roots` filtered them out, against its own comment ("EXCLUDED and counted"), help/fleet.md's "not dropped", and every other exclusion the sweep names (frozen, unreachable, failed). `audit` and `doc` list them apart.

Fix (the code, not the comment -- vc's ruling): `sweep_roots` lists every install with its kind, and `cmd_upgrade` names each worktree and dependency checkout in its not-swept table as `NOT AN ESTATE -- a worktree / a dependency checkout, not swept`; the summary line gains `N not an estate`. help/fleet.md says so. Tests: fleet.bats AT-3.2 is RESTATED -- it refuted the dep's name anywhere in the output, which pinned the silence itself; it now asserts the name is absent from the plan and present in the not-swept table -- plus a worktree arm; both driven red at the parent commit.


## Resolution

Fixed at `ab23ec4`, test driven red first at its parent commit. Full suite 1578/1579 at `ae3b200`: the one failing arm was environment-caused (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 exported in the running shell defeated readonlygit.bats' stale fixture, and its control arm caught it) and is green in a clean environment; that file is hardened at `ad86870`. Reviewed by vc against this issue; vc's mutants on 0099 and 0104 were killed. Ships in 0.1.4.
